title: Reciprocity
hook: The best way to get something from people is to give them something useful first, with no catch.
statement: When you give first, people naturally feel they want to give something back.
explainer: It's one of the deepest habits people have, in every culture. A real gift, like a free audit or an intro, builds goodwill. A cheap gift followed by a big ask backfires.
sop: List gifts that are valuable to them and cheap for you.
Keep the follow-up natural, not pushy.
Notice over time whether goodwill comes back.
Never pair a tiny gift with a huge ask.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Gift Value 7, Authenticity 9, Relevance 8. (7 + 9 + 8) ÷ 3 = 8.0. Higher means people will likely return the favor. Lower means it reads like a transaction and builds no real goodwill.
question: Pick one useful thing you can give a customer or partner this week, with no ask attached.
closing_statement: Give first without counting. The count happens anyway.
caption:
Principle Nº 299: Reciprocity

The best way to get something from people is to give them something useful first, with no catch.

When you give first, people naturally feel they want to give something back.

Your turn: Pick one useful thing you can give a customer or partner this week, with no ask attached.
